Course Title: Software Development using UML and Agile Methodology
description: The objective of this course is to prepare students for software development using UML and agile methodology.

syllabus.title: UML Fundamentals
syllabus.body: Overview of UML, modelling concepts - systems, models and views, data types, classes, abstract classes and objects, event classes, events and messages, object-oriented modelling. A deeper view: use case, object, class, sequence, collaboration, interaction overview, state machine, activity, component, deployment, package and timing diagrams.

syllabus.title: Agile Fundamentals
syllabus.body: What is Agile? Why Agile? Scrum, overview of PMI-ACP certification, the Agile Manifesto and its twelve principles. Agile concepts: Scrum, Extreme Programming, Test Driven Development, Continuous Integration, Refactoring, Pair Programming, Simple Design, User Stories, Agile Testing, Agile Tools, Burndown chart.

syllabus.title: Managing Projects with Scrum
syllabus.body: The rules of Scrum, Scrum roles – Product Owner, Scrum Master, Scrum Team, Scrum events, artifacts, product backlog, sprint backlog, user stories, sprint planning.

syllabus.title: Agile Software Development in Practice
syllabus.body: Lean Software Development, Kanban, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, Version Control. Using Patterns: what is a pattern, properties of patterns, Layer Pattern, Broker Pattern, Pipe and Filter Pattern, Model-View-Controller Pattern.

outcomes: Understand the concepts of UML and UML diagrams during object-oriented analysis and design.
Perform software development and process control using agile and scrum methodology.
Use tools and techniques such as Kanban, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack for Agile Software Development.
Justify designs based on design principles, patterns, and heuristics.
textbooks: Bernd Bruegge & Allen H. Dutoit, Object-Oriented Software Engineering Using UML, Patterns, and Java, Third Edition, Pearson.
Andrew Stellman & Jennifer Greene, Head First Agile, O'Reilly Media, 2017.
Len Bass, Paul Clements, Rick Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice, Pearson Education, Third edition, 2013.
referenceBooks: Ken Schawber, Mike Beedle, Agile Software Development with Scrum, Pearson, 2001.
